extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, scholars and policymakers interested in reparations, restorative justice, and public apologies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive criteria for what constitutes a public apology — its components, purposes, and roles within reparations and restorative justice contexts. Covers normative functions (healing, restoring social relations) and formal recognition (UN guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of wrongdoing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described on the page as one of the three components of the public apology process: the offender must acknowledge that a wrongdoing occurred. This is presented as a necessary first step in the restorative process (quoted as part of 'acknowledgment of wrongdoing, admission of responsibility and the action of the wrongdoer to compensate damages produced').

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the second component in the apology process. The offender must admit responsibility for the improper behavior or action, distinct from mere acknowledgment of facts. The page frames this as essential to reparative and restorative aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action to compensate damages produced
rubrics_metrics.description: The action of the wrongdoer to compensate damages produced
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The third component in the stated three-part process: beyond words, the wrongdoer should take action to compensate for harms caused. This ties the apology to material or practical reparative steps rather than symbolic language alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restorative purpose: healing and generating forgiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: A public apology is a restorative process intended to heal and to generate forgiveness on the part of the offended party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes that apologies are meant to restore moral relations between transgressors and victims. This criterion focuses on the intended outcome: healing, reconciliation, and eliciting forgiveness, rather than solely managing reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoring social interaction and affirming shared moral values
rubrics_metrics.description: Public apologies have the function of restoring the health of the social interaction and 'publicly acknowledging a shared commitment to some moral values'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective public apology should contribute to social repair by signalling a recommitment to shared norms and values. The page highlights this as a social-function criterion complementary to individual healing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commemoration or memorialization of history
rubrics_metrics.description: Commemorate or memorialize history as part of restorative action
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoting Cohen (2016), the page suggests that to restore or create moral relations, transgressors need to admit wrongdoing, 'commemorate or memorialize history', and provide an apology. This indicates that apology processes may appropriately include acts of remembrance or memorialization alongside admission and compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition as a component of reparations under UN guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Public apology is a component of reparation as stipulated in the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights resolution proclaiming the Basic Principles and Guidelines on the Right to a Remedy and Reparation for Victims of Gross Violations of International Human Rights Law and Serious Violations of International Humanitarian Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a formal/organizational standard: public apologies are recognized within UN reparations frameworks. For apologies undertaken in transitional justice or state-reparation contexts, aligning with UN guidance (acknowledgment, admission, compensation) is implied as a normative requirement.
